title: Age, Transfer & Excess-Shortage Problems
topic: Age Problems, Difference Unchanged, Give and Take, Excess and Shortage
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: A teacher has some sweets. If she gives 5 sweets to each pupil, she will have 12 sweets left. If she gives 7 sweets to each pupil, she will be short of 8 sweets. How many pupils are there?
questions.explanation: When giving 2 more sweets to each pupil (7 minus 5), the teacher uses up the 12 leftover sweets and needs 8 more sweets. Total sweets involved: 12 plus 8 equals 20 sweets. These 20 sweets are distributed as 2 extra sweets per pupil. Number of pupils: 20 divided by 2 equals 10 pupils.

questions.question: Maya is 14 years old. Her brother is 6 years old. How many years ago was Maya three times as old as her brother?
questions.explanation: The age difference between Maya and her brother never changes: 14 minus 6 equals 8 years. When Maya was three times as old as her brother, the difference of 8 years represents two equal parts (three parts minus one part). One part equals 8 divided by 2, which is 4 years. This was her brother's age at that time. Since he is now 6 years old, this happened 6 minus 4 equals 2 years ago. Check: Maya was 12, brother was 4, and 12 equals 3 times 4.

questions.question: There are some cookies to be shared. If each child gets 4 cookies, there will be 15 cookies left. If each child gets 6 cookies, there will be 3 cookies left. How many children are there?
questions.explanation: When giving 2 more cookies to each child (6 minus 4), the leftover cookies decrease by 12 (15 minus 3). These 12 extra cookies were used to give 2 more to each child. Number of children: 12 divided by 2 equals 6 children.

questions.question: Ryan has $96 and Sam has $48. Ryan gives some money to Sam so that Ryan has $24 more than Sam. How much did Ryan give?
questions.explanation: The total amount of money stays the same: $96 plus $48 equals $144. After the transfer, Ryan has $24 more than Sam. If we remove Ryan's extra $24 from the total, we get $144 minus $24 equals $120. This $120 is shared equally between them, so each has $60. Sam started with $48 and ended with $60, so Ryan gave him $60 minus $48 equals $12.

questions.question: A grandfather is 68 years old. His grandson is 8 years old. In how many years will the grandfather be 5 times as old as his grandson?
questions.explanation: The age difference never changes: 68 minus 8 equals 60 years. When the grandfather is five times as old as his grandson, the difference of 60 years represents four equal parts (five parts minus one part). One part equals 60 divided by 4, which is 15 years. This will be the grandson's age at that time. Since he is now 8 years old, this will happen in 15 minus 8 equals 7 years.

questions.question: Some pencils are to be distributed. If each student gets 3 pencils, 22 pencils remain. If each student gets 5 pencils, 4 pencils remain. How many pencils are there altogether?
questions.explanation: When giving 2 more pencils to each student (5 minus 3), the leftover pencils decrease by 18 (22 minus 4). These 18 extra pencils were used to give 2 more to each student. Number of students: 18 divided by 2 equals 9 students. Total pencils: 9 students times 3 pencils each plus 22 leftover equals 27 plus 22 equals 49 pencils.

questions.question: Cindy has 3 times as many books as David. If Cindy gives 18 books to David, they will have the same number of books. How many books did Cindy have at first?
questions.explanation: Cindy has three parts and David has one part, so the difference between them is two parts. When Cindy gives 18 books to David and they become equal, she has given away half of the original difference. Therefore, the original difference was 18 times 2 equals 36 books. Since the difference equals two parts, one part equals 36 divided by 2 equals 18 books. Cindy had three parts at first: 3 times 18 equals 54 books.

questions.question: A group of friends wants to buy a gift. If each contributes $8, they will be short of $10. If each contributes $10, they will have $6 extra. How many friends are there?
questions.explanation: When each friend contributes $2 more ($10 minus $8), the group changes from being $10 short to having $6 extra. This is a total swing of $16 ($10 plus $6). This $16 comes from each friend adding $2 more. Number of friends: $16 divided by $2 equals 8 friends.

questions.question: Alan is 5 years older than Ben. In 3 years, the sum of their ages will be 31 years. How old is Alan now?
questions.explanation: In 3 years, both Alan and Ben will be 3 years older, so together they will be 6 years older than now. Their total age now is 31 minus 6 equals 25 years. Alan is 5 years older than Ben. If we remove Alan's extra 5 years from the total, we get 25 minus 5 equals 20 years. This 20 years represents two equal ages, so Ben is 20 divided by 2 equals 10 years old now. Alan is 10 plus 5 equals 15 years old now.

questions.question: There are some oranges. If they are given 4 to each child, 14 oranges remain. If they are given 7 to each child, 2 oranges remain. How many oranges are there?
questions.explanation: When giving 3 more oranges to each child (7 minus 4), the leftover oranges decrease by 12 (14 minus 2). These 12 extra oranges were used to give 3 more to each child. Number of children: 12 divided by 3 equals 4 children. Total oranges: 4 children times 4 oranges each plus 14 leftover equals 16 plus 14 equals 30 oranges. Check: 4 children times 7 oranges equals 28, plus 2 leftover equals 30 oranges.

questions.question: Some cupcakes are packed into boxes. If 5 cupcakes are packed in each box, 8 cupcakes are left unpacked. If 8 cupcakes are packed in each box, 2 cupcakes are left unpacked. How many cupcakes are there?
questions.explanation: The number of boxes stays the same. When packing 3 more cupcakes per box (8 minus 5), the leftover cupcakes decrease by 6 (8 minus 2). These 6 extra cupcakes were used to pack 3 more into each box. Number of boxes: 6 divided by 3 equals 2 boxes. Total cupcakes: 2 boxes times 5 cupcakes each plus 8 leftover equals 10 plus 8 equals 18 cupcakes. Check: 2 boxes times 8 cupcakes equals 16, plus 2 leftover equals 18 cupcakes.

questions.question: A coach has some basketballs. If he gives 3 basketballs to each team, he will have 9 basketballs left. If he gives 5 basketballs to each team, he will have 1 basketball left. How many teams are there?
questions.explanation: When giving 2 more basketballs to each team (5 minus 3), the leftover basketballs decrease by 8 (9 minus 1). These 8 extra basketballs were used to give 2 more to each team. Number of teams: 8 divided by 2 equals 4 teams.
